question.problem: A math teacher split their calculus class into two groups, Group $A$ and Group $B.$ Group $A$ has $43%$ of the total number of students, while Group $B$ has $57%$ of the total number of students. If $23%$ of the students in Group $A$ obtained the top grade, and $19%$ of the students in Group $B$ obtained the top grade, what is the probability that a randomly selected student from either group obtained the top grade?
question.worked_solution:
Let $G$ be the event that the chosen student obtained the top grade, and let $A$ be the event that the student is from Group $A.$ Then, ${A}^{′}$ is the event that the student is from Group $B.$

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected student obtained the top grade, we can use the law of total probability:

$$
P(G)=P(G|A)P(A)+P(G|{A}^{′})P({A}^{′})
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each bit of information into mathematical notation.

- Since $43%$ of their students are in Group $A$ and $57%$ are in Group $B$, we have

$$
P(A)=0.43,\,P({A}^{′})=0.57.
$$

- Since $23%$ of the students in Group $A$ obtained the top grade and $19%$ of the students in Group $B$ obtained the top grade, we have

$$
P(G|A)=0.23,\,P(G|{A}^{′})=0.19.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability that a randomly selected student from either group obtained the top grade

$$
\begin{aligned}P(G) & =P(G|A)P(A)+P(G|{A}^{′})P({A}^{′}) \\  & =(0.23)(0.43)+(0.19)(0.57) \\  & ≈0.207\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
